text.p: Chances of any delay in a Polish general election on September 21 because of catastrophic floods faded on Friday after the co-ruling Peasant Party decided against supporting an opposition motion to declare a state of emergency.
The right-wing and centrist opposition demanded that the state of emergency be imposed in the south and west of the country, a move which would automatically lead to the vote being postponed.
Some Peasant Party officials earlier said they favoured delaying the polls, but the party leadership decided on Friday it would not back the opposition motion.
"The state of emergency is a thing of the past, because the flood is going away," Peasant leader Waldemar Pawlak told a news conference.
President Aleksander Kwasniewski, the only person authorised by law to declare the state of emergency, has also said he was against the move unless the deluge returns.

The biggest party in the ruling coalition, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), has always abjected to delaying the polls, in which they hope to defeat its main challenger, the Solidarity Election Action alliance (AWS).
